title: Choose Kinward's new look
question: Same words and same facts, a more technical and professional look. Pick one, steer it, or ask for another hand.

options.label: Signal Wayfinding
options.lineage: Modern hospital and airport signage systems
options.thesis: One post, signposted to everywhere it went, like a building that tells you exactly where to go.
options.viewport: A graphite sign panel fills the first screen: the headline, then three routed rows with arrows and live status.
options.risk: Can feel cool for a hospitality buyer unless the photos stay warm.

raised.raise: Every number owns a fixed place, so 214 families reads like an instrument, not a slogan.
One accent color is reserved for whatever is live right now.

options.label: Network Map
options.thesis: Your community is the station; every family, page and printout is a stop on the line.
options.viewport: Deep navy, headline left, a route map running off the right edge from One post out to Website, Text, Email and Print.
options.risk: Technical network diagrams are a familiar tech-company move, and this is the closest of the three to it.

options.label: Living Field
options.lineage: Experiential studio sites with full-screen animated color
options.thesis: A slow, breathing color field behind large type: the most obviously tech of the set.
options.viewport: Full-screen indigo field moving slowly, one large headline, product panels floating over it.
options.case: Reads as tech instantly, but older buyers lose some clarity and it depends most on motion.
options.risk: Least hospitable to older readers, and text over motion is the hardest to keep readable.

options.label: Laboratory Counter
options.lineage: Glowing tube counters on lab instruments
options.thesis: Every count shown as glowing digits.
options.viewport: Banks of glowing digits counting families reached.
options.case: Too retro and too dark for this buyer, and there are few real numbers to show.
options.kept: Every number owns a fixed place.

options.label: Hand-Processed Film
options.thesis: Community life as frames on a strip.
options.viewport: A film strip of community moments.
options.case: Artistic rather than technical, and it hides the offer.
options.kept: One accent reserved for what is live.

options.label: Coiled Earth
options.thesis: A page built up in earthen courses.
options.case: The opposite of the technical look you asked for.
options.kept: Text measures that match their container exactly.

options.label: Pixel Metropolis
options.thesis: A community as a zoomable pixel city.
options.viewport: A dense pixel city of residents and staff.
options.case: Playful and saturated, so not professional for this buyer.
options.kept: One shared grid for every object.

options.label: Lowbrow Panel
options.viewport: A packed airbrushed panel with a hand-lettered title.
options.case: Wrong audience and wrong tone entirely.
options.kept: Clear active state on whatever is selected.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean software-company homepage, done very well.
canonCard.viewport: White page, headline and buttons on the left, a product screen on the right.
canonCard.risk: Looks like most software sites by design.
